label: 6d — Vacuity Audit (Dafny + Isabelle)
summary: 3 blocking vacuity signal(s) detected (plus 1 advisory). The corresponding verifier passes discharge `True` obligations and do not establish behavioural content.

issues.title: [BLOCKING] Dafny Valid() body is literally `true` (or empty) and no other behavioural ensures clauses are active
issues.fix_directive:
Every `ensures Valid()` clause in the generated Dafny is equivalent to `ensures true` while Valid() returns true, AND no per-transition behavioural `ensures` clauses are active (the template emits them as comments). The Dafny verifier therefore discharges only `ensures true` obligations — `0 errors` does not establish behavioural correctness, only well-formedness.

To make Dafny verification load-bearing, the M2T-Dafny template (forge.transformations/src/main/resources/transformations/java2dafny.egl) must either: (a) derive a non-trivial Valid() body from the requirements, or (b) emit per-transition `ensures` clauses as ACTIVE obligations rather than comments. (b) is the more direct route to behavioural verification.

issues.title: [BLOCKING] Precondition of zoperation Idle_Analysis is unsatisfiable
issues.raw: pre "st= Analysis \<and> \<not>(sts= (noGas)) \<and> \<not>(sts= (gasD))"  -- enum lens `sts` has no admissible value left (last atom: `! (sts= (gasD))`)
issues.fix_directive: The precondition of `Idle_Analysis` can never hold (enum lens `sts` has no admissible value left (last atom: `! (sts= (gasD))`)), so every proof obligation about this operation is vacuously true and the operation can never fire. The extractor prepends the negations of every EARLIER branch guard in the same mode (faithful else-if semantics), so a contradiction here almost always means the SOURCE JAVA TRANSITION IS DEAD CODE: an earlier branch in the same mode has a guard that subsumes or equals part of this branch's guard, so this branch can never be reached. FIX IN THE JAVA: find this operation's source branch via the traceability entry, compare its guard with the earlier branches in the same mode, and reorder the branches (most-specific first) or merge them per the requirements' intent. Do NOT touch any .egl template. Only if the named atoms are NOT equivalent in the Java (i.e. the contradiction was introduced by extraction, not by branch ordering) is this an instrument issue — report it to the operator instead of editing anything.

issues.title: [ADVISORY] Idle operation Idle_Analysis is unreachable: the mode's branches are exhaustive
issues.raw: pre "st= Analysis \<and> \<not>(sts= (noGas)) \<and> \<not>(sts= (gasD))"  -- offered={}: UNSAT (enum lens `sts` has no admissible value left (last atom: `! (sts= (gasD))`))
issues.fix_directive: ADVISORY — no action for the codegen agent. This follows from the deliberate CSP domain narrowing (FDR4 finiteness), not from the Java. Record it with any verdict drawn from the CSP checks.

issues.title: [BLOCKING] Mode(s) unreachable from Init in the symbolic model: Avoiding, AvoidingAgain, Final, Found, GettingOut, Going, TryingAgain
issues.fix_directive: No sequence of operations reaches these modes even with unnarrowed numeric domains and uninterpreted functions. Any invariant lemma about them is vacuous. Check the transition extraction for the missing edges.

next_step: Strengthen the flagged template(s) so the verifier discharges behavioural obligations rather than `True`. Until that is done, do not count the corresponding verifier pass as evidence of behavioural correctness in the experiment write-up.
